⚡ SNF PULSE™

INSTITUTIONAL POSITIONING

BERKSHIRE CUT CAPITAL ONE 62%. DELTA AND HOUSING WENT THE OTHER DIRECTION.

Berkshire Hathaway's newly filed Q3 holdings show a selective change in capital allocation under CEO Greg Abel.

WHAT CHANGED

🔴 Capital One: Stake reduced 62% to 1.15 million shares.
🔴 Bank of America: Stake reduced 6% to 455.9 million shares.
🟢 Delta Air Lines: Stake increased 12% to 64.45 million shares.
🟢 Lennar: Position roughly doubled.

WHY IT MATTERS

Berkshire is reducing selected financial exposures while adding to businesses tied to travel and housing demand.

But this is not a wholesale retreat from banks. Bank of America remains one of Berkshire's largest holdings.

The filing reflects September 30 positions, not today's trades.

WHAT SNF IS WATCHING

Whether Berkshire continues trimming banks, adds further housing exposure, or changes its positioning as credit conditions and consumer demand evolve.

SNF LENS™

🟢 Signal: Confirmed changes in Berkshire's Q3 holdings.
⚪ Noise: Quarterly disclosures do not establish current positions or investment motives.
🟡 Confirmation: Subsequent filings showing sustained allocation changes.
🔴 Risk: Economic sensitivity in airlines, housing and credit.

BOTTOM LINE

Berkshire is not abandoning financials. It is becoming more selective about where it commits capital.

Innerhalb weniger Stunden legen parallele Systemstörungen im US Finanzsektor und im Luftverkehr offen, wie eng vernetzt und zugleich störanfällig digitale Kernprozesse geworden sind.

Am Montag traten bei führenden US Geldhäusern wie JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, U.S. Bank und Capital One sowie beim Zahlungsdienst Zelle spürbare Ausfälle beim Onlinebanking und im Zahlungsverkehr auf, was JPMorgan Chase auf einen internen Softwarefehler bei eigenen Systemen zurückführte, der auch Transaktionen mit Partnerbanken verzögerte. Nahezu zeitgleich meldete United Airlines eine landesweite Systemstörung bei der Berechnung von Flugzeuggewichten, die Abflüge nur wenige Tage nach dem großen FAA Flugstopp erneut ausbremste, inzwischen jedoch laut Unternehmensangaben behoben wurde.

Selbst wenn beide Vorfälle offiziell als unabhängige technische Probleme ohne Hinweise auf Cyberangriffe eingestuft werden, zeigt die rasche Abfolge solcher Störungen ein erhebliches Klumpenrisiko im Alltag kritischer Infrastruktur. Sobald einzelne Softwarefehler im Interbankengeschäft sofort auf mehrere Institute übergreifen und Airlines unmittelbar nach behördlichen Systemausfällen erneut am Boden bleiben, gerät das Vertrauen in die digitale Betriebssicherheit unter spürbaren Druck.

Wie lassen sich interne IT Updates und Schnittstellen im Bankwesen sowie in der Luftfahrt besser absichern, damit einzelne Softwarefehler nicht mehr sofort Kettenreaktionen über ganze Branchen auslösen?

#GeoFinanceNow #Finanzmaerkte #Infrastruktur #Luftfahrt

🚨 This is highly unusual.

Some of the largest banks in the United States have all gone down at the same time.

This afternoon, customers of JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and U.S. Bank were unable to log into their online accounts.

Before you try opening your banking app again, read this first.

Nearly 4,800 reports.

That is the number of incident reports submitted by JPMorgan Chase customers to Downdetector as of 2:00 PM Eastern Time, involving:

→ Failed logins
→ Apps failing to load
→ Bank of America displaying “System currently down”
→ Wells Fargo displaying “Online banking is temporarily unavailable”

Now, let’s connect the dots:

→ Thursday: Microsoft 365 goes down.
→ Friday: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issues a nationwide ground stop, halting all flights across the United States.
→ Saturday: Microsoft restores its services.
→ Monday: JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Wells Fargo, and U.S. Bank are paralyzed.
→ Customers of Truist Bank, Zelle, and Capital One also report issues.
→ JPMorgan Chase confirms they are addressing a problem.

But the banks are only part of the issue.

→ Customers cannot check their balances.
→ There are reports that some branches are unable to provide cash to customers.
→ No cause has been announced.
→ No timeline for a full resolution has been provided.

This is certainly not a routine incident.

This marks the third time in five days that a nationwide outage has occurred, affecting systems that Americans rely on every single day.

Most people are not prepared for what might happen next. When it happens, it might no longer be “just an incident.”

Paychecks, bills, and bank transfers could all get stuck at the same time.

If you aren’t following me yet, you’re going to regret it.
